thread:
Maya (Design): Quick accessibility pass on the Settings panel (switches + form helpers). Found a couple of small but important issues — posting findings and proposed fixes.
Ravi (Frontend): thanks, drop them in — can triage next sprint.
Maya (Design): 1) Screen reader verbosity on the toggle control: NVDA/VoiceOver reads "Toggle" then the label, then "button". This is noisy. We should use `role="switch"` and `aria-checked` instead of a bare button. Example: `button role="switch" aria-checked="false" aria-labelledby="notify-label"`.
Jamal (QA): I can repro this — VoiceOver says "Button, Notifications, button". Using role=switch should get it to read "Notifications, off" which is better.
Maya (Design): 2) Helper text isn't tied to the control via aria-describedby. Screen readers skip the helper so users miss the quota note under API keys. We should add `aria-describedby` with the helper id.
Eli (Eng): quick question — for the helper text approach, do we keep visible helper copy or put it in `sr-only` for mobile condensed layout? Might affect layout.
Maya (Design): keep visible on desktop. For condensed mobile view, show the same text but collapse visually and keep `aria-describedby` so SRs still announce it.
Ravi (Frontend): noted. We'll add `aria-describedby` and ensure the helper id is unique. Also will update tests.
Maya (Design): 3) Focus ring clipping: the toggle live region is inside an overflow:hidden container; when you tab to it the focus ring gets cut off. We should move focusable controls out of the clipping container or adjust CSS: `.control-container { overflow: visible; }` or ensure `outline-offset` to keep ring inside.
Jamal (QA): I saw keyboard users losing the focus outline when switching between sections — it's a usability regression from the recent layout tweak.
Ravi (Frontend): I'll try `outline-offset` first to avoid restructuring DOM, but if that creates layout issues we'll revisit container overflow.
Maya (Design): 4) Contrast: the disabled toggle thumb (light gray on slightly darker gray) fails 4.5:1 for body text. Need to bump to a darker disabled state. I'll attach a tiny palette suggestion in the thread.
accessibility-bot: Contrast check: current color pair #bdbdbd on #e9e9e9 => AA fail for 14px text (ratio 2.1:1). Recommendation: #9b9b9b on #e9e9e9 => contrast 4.6:1.
Sophie (Product): Is the new disabled color still visually subtle? We want to keep disabledness clear but meet contrast.
Maya (Design): yes — tested a few steps darker, still reads as disabled because opacity + thumb shape cues remain. I'll add a mockup to Figma.
Eli (Eng): estimated frontend work: role changes + aria-describedby + contrast tweak + focus fix => 4 engineer-days including tests. Sounds fine for next sprint.
Ravi (Frontend): I'll create a PR with: 1) change role/aria attributes, 2) aria-describedby hookup, 3) CSS fix for outline-offset and disabled colors, 4) unit + axe checks.
Jamal (QA): I'll add VoiceOver/NVDA checks to the regression QA checklist and run keyboard-only flows.
Maya (Design): thanks — small wins but important. Can we aim to ship these before the Dedicated rollout? Accessibility regressions would be bad in that release.
Sophie (Product): prioritizing this as P1 for the Dedicated release branch. Ravi, assign an owner and estimated completion date?
Ravi (Frontend): assigning to me. Will open a draft PR by EOD tomorrow and set target merge by next Wed.
Maya (Design): awesome — ping me on the PR for review. Also tagging the UX handbook entry to include the `role=switch` pattern.
accessibility-bot: Automated note: remember to run `npm run a11y:ci` in the PR to surface any regressions.
Maya (Design): thanks all :raised_hands:
